caption: The drawing is a technical diagram of a wooden chest, labeled “Dower Chest, Yellow Pine,” from Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, circa 1780. The image is monochromatic, rendered in black ink on a light tan or cream background. The composition consists of three main detailed views: a top view, a front elevation, and a side elevation. The top view is a simple rectangle representing the chest's lid, annotated with the word “TOP” and dimensions, specifically 52 1/2 inches by 23 1/4 inches, with a latch or keyhole detail. The front elevation shows the chest’s decorative panel with three large, rounded arches above rectangular panels, each arch measuring 9 1/2 inches across and 4 3/4 inches high, surrounded by measured notations for the widths and spacing of each section. The lower part of the front contains additional measurements for the base and feet. The side elevation shows a single arch panel, with the chest’s depth (22 1/2 inches) and height (24 inches) clearly marked. The image includes precise dimensions in inches for most parts and uses cross-hatching for shaded areas. In the upper right corner, a boxed text panel provides provenance information, including the donor's name (Mrs. Robert W. de Forest), date (1933), location (Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York City), and the name of the draftsman (Michael Trekur). The lower left corner contains a scale bar noting “3/8” to 1 inch.”
title: Pa. German Dower Chest
